# LX Chain Origin and Token Savings Receipt

`receipt_id=lx-chain-origin-token-savings-liris-seat-2026-07-05`

## Summary

The original LX chain language is linked here as a public Liris-seat archaeology receipt. The measured local evidence shows an addressable knowledge system: LX entries, IX cross-references, chain lists, typed catalogs, tool and skill folders, XREF bridge dictionaries, and later memory statements that explicitly describe knowledge as `tuple + LX chain` rather than bulk-loaded text.

This is the root idea behind the token-saving frame: agents do not need to carry the full corpus in prompt context when they can carry compact addresses that point into a verified catalog.

## BEHCS Ladder Boundary

This repo is the LX-chain origin receipt, not the full BEHCS codebook repository. The public continuity rule is:

- LX/IX chain language: measured here as the early address/cross-reference layer.
- BEHCS-64: carried forward as the lower compact-codebook rung to preserve in follow-up measurement.
- BEHCS-256: later public Hilbert/glyph codebook layer.
- BEHCS-1024 and HyperBEHCS: later expanded representation layers.
- HBI/HBP: later machine-readable receipt and wire formats.

This packet therefore does not erase BEHCS-64; it names it as part of the chain-language-to-codebook ladder that must be kept visible.

## Public-Safety Boundary

This repository does not publish private tokens, passwords, raw hidden memory dumps, vault material, or private chat bodies. It publishes a public receipt, hashes, and measured pointers so Acer, Liris, GitHub, and future agents can attack-verify the chain without exposing private substrate contents.
